memories.content: Avoid em dashes in the proposal; split the sentence or use more ordinary punctuation instead.
The user tends to place several independently reviewable claims in one long sentence.
Use first-person active voice for choices and commitments owned by the proposal author so responsibility remains explicit throughout the work plan.
Describe prototype operations that have already been implemented and verified as observed states.
Describe prototype operations not yet implemented or evaluated as plans or expectations.
When a commitment is phrased passively, readers may interpret it as uncertainty, evasiveness, or reluctance to take responsibility.
Use “we” only for decisions and commitments the authors control, not for external facts or actions owned by another party.
The user should use one first-person pronoun consistently for the same authorial role and should not alternate between “I” and “we” unless the responsible party actually changes.
The user tends to hide unsettled commitments behind passive phrases such as “will be considered” or “is expected.”
Split proposal prose into short sentences when a sentence contains more than one independently reviewable claim.
Keep one main claim in each sentence so a reviewer can locate and assess it quickly.
The user tends to repeat em dashes when a sentence already contains several clauses.
Repeated em dashes can shift a reviewer’s attention from the proposal’s argument to suspicion that its prose was generated by AI.
Link anticipated participant burden with its mitigation strategies for each field user study task.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the field system and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided in the field user study.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately upon collection.
List equipment to be loaned when participants lack necessary gear.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
The HCI ethics reviewer verifies that anticipated burden and mitigation strategies correspond for each field user study task.
Ensure that participants can safely return to existing work procedures if they discontinue research participation.
Specify that organizational members who decline research participation will not face disadvantages in task assignment or performance evaluation.
The user's withdrawal risk can be adequately assessed only when a safe alternative procedure exists for field tasks.
The user tends to assume that a short session also entails little burden from work interruption and exposure to a manager.

analysis.overview: The frames contain independent guidance: the reference addresses proposal style, authorial responsibility, and evidential phrasing, while the compared frame addresses field-study ethics, participant protections, accessibility, data handling, and equipment logistics. No supplied claims govern the same operational decision.

relations.reason: These reference-only memories state the tendency, editing rule, and reviewer-facing rationale for one punctuation policy; the compared frame has no corresponding claim.
relations.summary: Proposal prose should avoid repeated em dashes, particularly in clause-heavy sentences, because they distract reviewers and may evoke AI-generated writing.

relations.reason: These reference-only memories describe the observed long-sentence tendency and split one corrective rule about sentence-level claim granularity; the compared frame does not address prose structure.
relations.summary: Proposal prose should place independently reviewable claims in separate, short sentences so each main claim is easy to locate and assess.

relations.reason: These reference-only memories provide the behavior, policy, and rationale for explicitly owning proposal commitments; no compared memory addresses authorial voice.
relations.summary: Author-controlled choices and commitments should use first-person active voice because passive formulations can conceal unsettled responsibility and signal uncertainty or evasion.

relations.reason: The two reference-only memories split one status-sensitive wording rule across its explicit verified and unverified conditions; the compared frame has no prototype-status claim.
relations.summary: Prototype operations should be described as observed states when implemented and verified, but as plans or expectations when not yet implemented or evaluated.

relations.reason: This is independently useful reference-only guidance about the ownership scope of “we,” with no corresponding compared claim.
relations.summary: The pronoun “we” should be reserved for decisions and commitments controlled by the authors, excluding external facts and actions owned by others.

relations.reason: This is independently useful reference-only guidance about stable authorial identity, distinct from whether a particular action is author-controlled and absent from the compared frame.
relations.summary: A single first-person pronoun should be used consistently for the same authorial role, changing between “I” and “we” only when responsibility changes.

relations.reason: These compared-only memories split one task-level burden-and-mitigation requirement into proposal content and reviewer verification; the reference frame has no field-study burden policy.
relations.summary: Each field-study task should pair anticipated participant burden with corresponding mitigation strategies, enabling the ethics reviewer to verify that correspondence.

relations.reason: These compared-only memories split one accessibility requirement into identifying necessary accommodations and describing their delivery; the reference frame has no accessibility claim.
relations.summary: The field study should specify both the accommodations participants need to access the system and research tasks and how those accommodations will be provided.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-only data-handling protection with no corresponding reference claim.
relations.summary: Personal identifiers should be separated from research data immediately when the data are collected.

relations.reason: These compared-only memories split one equipment-loan logistics requirement into provision and return components; the reference frame does not address participant equipment.
relations.summary: The study should identify equipment loaned to participants who lack necessary gear and describe the procedure for returning it.

relations.reason: These compared-only memories state the operational safeguard and its assessment significance as parts of one withdrawal-protection claim; the reference frame has no withdrawal policy.
relations.summary: Field participation requires a safe alternative work procedure so participants who withdraw can return to existing practices and withdrawal risk can be assessed adequately.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful compared-only protection against workplace consequences, with no corresponding reference claim.
relations.summary: Organizational members who decline research participation should face no disadvantage in task assignment or performance evaluation.

relations.reason: This compared-only memory identifies a specific recurring assessment error that remains independently useful beyond the general burden-mitigation requirement; the reference frame has no counterpart.
relations.summary: Short study sessions should not be assumed to impose little burden because work interruption and exposure to a manager may still create meaningful risks.

reports.compared_only: The compared frame covers task-level burden mitigation, accessibility, identifier separation, equipment loans, safe withdrawal procedures, protection for nonparticipants, and overlooked workplace pressures.
reports.reference_only: The reference emphasizes concise, reviewable sentences, restrained punctuation, explicit authorial ownership, consistent pronouns, and wording that distinguishes verified prototype behavior from future plans.
